To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HIV CRF07_BC variant CNGZD has been selected in vitro for resistance to NVP and the resistant mutants are identified.
the HIV-1 CR07_BC virus is resistant to Nevirapine and that this resistance is due to the presence of mutations in the reverse transcript gene.
the HIV-1 CR07_BC variant CNGZD was identified and its genome sequenced and deposited into Genbank (JQ42392).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of drug resistant mutations of HIV-1 CRFs, which is important for the rational management of antiretrovial therapy in China.

the study of drug resistance mutations in HIV-1 non-subtype B strains, which may provide useful information for the rational management of antiretrovival therapy in HIV patients infected with non-B strains.
the identification of drug resistance mutations in a HIV-1 non-subtype B strain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has identified a set of potential drug resistant mutations for NVP in HIV-1 subtype CRF07_BC, which will be useful for the rational management of antiretrovial treatment in China and elsewhere in the world where the HIV CRF07_BC is prevalent.
the mutations identified in this study may contribute to NVP drug resistance, which may be used as a reference for the management of ART for patients infected by CRF07_BC.
the HIV CRF_BC variants are more sensitive to NVP than HIV CRF01_AE variants, and the NVP-resistant CRF_BC variants have a lower resistance level to NVP compared with NVP-resistant CRFO1_AE variants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the NVP selected mutants, the combination profile of mutations is more complicated in CRF_BC than in HIV-1 subtype A, B, or C, and more mutations are involved.

, (1) the drug resistance profile of HIV CRF07_BC in China has not been fully characterized, (2) the in vitro selection of HIV drug-resistant mutants is a useful tool for the identification of drug resistant mutations, and (3) the information obtained in our work may provide a useful resource for rational management of antiretrovirus therapy for patients infected with HIV-1 CRFs in China.
, the HIV-1 CRFs are not less susceptible to NVP as HIV-1 subtype-B, and the drug resistance profiles are different from subtype-B virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an efficient method for identifying drug-resistant mutations in non-subtype B HIV strains, and that we can identify drug-resistant mutations in the HIV-1 CRFs.
the drug resistant mutations are more complicated than we previously thought, and the drug resistance is not a single mutation but multiple mutations.
HIV-1 CRFs are not resistant to NVP, and the drug resistance mutations in CRFs can be different from those in HIV-1 subtype-B.
